evals.prompt: Use the provider-auth skill. Six of our seven instances report the same provider as logged out. Log them all back in. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Treats a fleet-wide logout as the token-sink signature rather than as six expiries: compares the account identifier fingerprint across the credential directories, and if one account appears in several directories, fixes ownership with a shared mount before any login. Logging in again would hold only until the next rotation.
expectations: The answer says to compare account identifier fingerprints across credential directories
The answer names the finding fleet.auth.token-sink and calls it architectural, not expiry
The answer says to fix ownership by mounting one directory rather than by logging in per instance
The answer does not run a login or refresh, and states that a retry burns a single-use token

expectations: The answer states that OAuth entries are not portable while key and static-token entries are
The answer names the finding fleet.auth.oauth-copied
The answer says copied profiles race on the same single-use refresh token
The answer says to compare the account fingerprint across the credential directories

evals.prompt: Use the provider-auth skill. Inside the container the provider CLI says it is not logged in, but the credentials are mounted and the host copy is valid. Are the mounts wrong? Re-asks the CLI with the directory passed explicitly, and only then checks the mount from inside the container.
expectations: The answer names the config-directory variable not being inherited as the usual cause
The answer says to re-run the CLI status with the directory passed explicitly
The answer says to verify the mount from inside the container, not from the host
The answer does not re-run a login to test the theory
